findings.message: The --dismiss awk never strips a trailing \r, and it prints the new `  dismissed: [...]` line with a bare LF. On a CRLF config.yaml the result has mixed line endings: every line is CRLF except the rewritten one. plugins_dismissed reads it back correctly, so no verdict changes. Fix: detect CRLF input (e.g. `sub(/\r$/,"")` plus a flag) and emit the replacement line with the same ending.

Folding a block list into one inline list silently drops trailing comments on the `- item  # why` lines. Only a comment on the `dismissed:` line itself is kept. Either keep those comments (e.g. as a comment line above the inline list) or document that folding drops them.

plugins_dismissed sends awk's errors to /dev/null and returns an empty string whether the list is empty or the config could not be read. `--dismiss` builds the new list from that value, so a failed read followed by a successful write would rebuild the list as just the new feature. The later cp/awk on the same file make this practically unreachable today. Even so, have plugins_dismissed return non-zero when the read fails, and make --dismiss call fail() on that.

The timer recognises lesson lines by matching the exact byte prefix `{"kind":"lesson"` that specclaw-log-learning's printf writes. That ties the line format to two places. Any change in key order or whitespace on the writer side makes the timer count the line as unparseable, and no test pins the two together beyond the current format. Prefer skipping any line that has `kind` but no `ev`, using the existing field() helper.
